system.name: PytyRe
system.principle: Development in either component is development of the unified PytyRe system. Every change is reviewed against both sides and their shared contracts.

ownership.contract: Reaper is the canonical owner of .rpr syntax and language semantics; Pytyliki consumes versioned language and semantic interfaces rather than maintaining a competing parser.
Reaper owns canonical typed IR, source locations, diagnostics and compiler-stage contracts; processor-domain operations must lower through versioned Reaper interfaces.
Reaper owns compiler/runtime semantics and native ABI. Native compiler parity and full self-hosting remain separately tracked.
Pytyliki owns processor engineering workflows, architecture models, ISA and microarchitecture tooling, processor evidence and validation.
Pytyliki owns native processor discovery, bounded measurements, numerical metric services, embedded target profiles and low-level target contracts.
Reaper expresses typed/effect-checked intent; Pytyliki validates processor and target constraints. Actual device access remains delegated to an explicitly supplied trusted host backend.

interfaces.activation: Reaper requires an explicit absolute library path and explicit --allow-native-ffi permission.
constraints: The library is trusted native code and is never discovered implicitly.
Calls are synchronous, bounded and do not retain caller-owned buffers.
Metadata discovery does not load or execute plugin code.
Provider exports do not imply that every operation is currently wrapped by Reaper's high-level adapter.

interfaces.activation: A trusted local Reaper checkout is supplied explicitly with -DREAPER_SOURCE_DIR=/absolute/path/to/Reaper.
constraints: The Reaper C17 ABI is linked at build time; there is no runtime library search.
The bridge exposes the bounded Reaper i64 expression evaluator and exact lookup only.
A build without REAPER_SOURCE_DIR remains self-contained and reports the backend as unavailable.
The wrapper forwards Reaper ABI statuses unchanged when the linked ABI is available.

development_policy.change_rule: Every change in Reaper or Pytyliki must include a reciprocal impact review. When a shared contract, ABI, syntax, IR, target model or safety boundary changes, update and test both repositories in coordinated PRs.
development_policy.integration_rule: Keep one canonical implementation for each owned subsystem. Share through typed/versioned contracts and native adapters; do not fork competing parsers, runtimes or processor models.
development_policy.synchronization_rule: Update the shared contract and both pinned integration workflows together when either side changes an exposed ABI.
development_policy.release_rule: A PytyRe release is qualified only when both component revisions and both reciprocal integration test paths are recorded.

safety_boundaries: Native FFI is opt-in and loads only a caller-selected trusted library.
The Reaper native bridge evaluates a bounded integer expression; it is not a general-purpose execution sandbox.
The Pytyliki-to-Reaper bridge links only the explicit Reaper C ABI at build time.
The low-level hardware contract has no default physical backend; no driver installation, firmware flashing, physical MMIO write or privileged operation is implied.
The existing Pytyliki vendor/reaper_frontend snapshot is an expression-only frontend with retained Apache-2.0 provenance; it is not a copy of the complete Reaper compiler or runtime.
Component licenses remain distinct. Preserve MIT and Apache-2.0 notices for their respective works and all vendor attribution.
known_gaps: Reaper native compiler parity and full self-hosting are incomplete.
The vendored Reaper frontend in Pytyliki handles tokenization and a single expression, not full .rpr program execution.
Processor physical models and low-level hardware APIs remain capability- and backend-gated; no physical backend is shipped.
Some Pytyliki ABI provider operations are available to C consumers but are not yet exposed as dedicated high-level Reaper builtins.
